q: What is the Revolution of Values?
a: In Playing Qortal, the Revolution of Values is a quiet change of heart: from greed for money and profit toward sharing without expecting return. Not weapons or governments. Your time is priceless; Qortal records it as QORT by keeping a computer on a shared network. When enough refuse to sell that time for money, kindness remains—#QQQ. Take what resonates; leave the rest.

No. Qortal the network is not a video game—it is real decentralized software and community infrastructure. When Playing Qortal says "game," it is a metaphor for the Revolution of Values: voluntary participation, golden rules, winning together by valuing time and kindness over money. Ordinary life is the board—not a console title.

An invitation to join a voluntary real network while practicing kinder values—minting time as QORT, showing up as a human, widening free kindness (#QQQ). Metaphorically: walk out of musical-chairs money and build a room with a chair for everyone. Not high scores; time, sovereignty, community.

#QQQ is the book's real currency of New Earth: kind words and acts never billed—Here, this is for you; I'm sorry; I forgive you; Thank you; How are you? Everyone already mints it; widen the circle from family to the whole human family. Free software culture is proof it can work at scale.

q: Take what resonates—what does that mean?
a: Simon James offers invitation, not creed: take what resonates, gently leave the rest. Nothing asks belief; look and decide. Reject every spiritual page and still use Qortal as honest private infrastructure. Philosophy is why he does it—not a toll at the door.

Not another planet—this Earth lived differently. Tribes of a few hundred, Community Centers of welcome, Local Groups into an ICF that serves never rules, land healed by care, Tribe energy and water, pay in #QQQ. Stars to steer by, not a stamped blueprint. Start: garden, neighbor, node, kindness.

Self-sufficient sovereign communities of a few hundred at most—about as many faces as the heart holds (Dunbar ~150). Everyone knows everyone; sharing is baseline like a newborn. Connected freely; not ruled from above. All for one, one for all.

One great building at each Tribe's heart: school, sport, saunas, cold pools, workshops, long kitchens, clinic, traveler rooms, tools and books lent freely—owned by none, belonging to all. The new church. Only prayer: come in, you are welcome, take what you need.

Integral Collective Federation—vision for Tribes connecting across Earth post-money. A hundred Tribes make a Local Group: city with no seat of power, only sharing. Fresco/Peter Joseph spirit, but decentralized: join and leave freely; serves Tribes, never rules. Tool, never throne.

q: Build beside the old—what does that mean?
a: We do not have to overthrow anything. Build the better thing quietly beside the old and walk through—brick by brick, Tribe by Tribe—until one morning old rooms have emptied. Krishnamurti: no measure of health to be well adjusted to a profoundly sick society.

That one word—voluntary—carries the transformation. Qortal never requires buying, selling, or permission. Forced values would be the old game in new clothes. Voluntary cooperation keeps #QQQ authentic and sovereignty yours.

Your time, keys, and voice are yours: mint on your machine, hold your secret phrase, need no gatekeeper papers, help run an internet no company owns. Guard privacy; be wary of systems promising owning nothing will make you happy while others mean to own a great deal.

q: What is the book's financial advice?
a: Never be fearful and never be greedy. Not telling you to buy, sell, or get rich—measuring life in currency is the trap. Minted QORT is a reserve of time; sell only if necessity leaves no choice. No first-mover advantage money can buy.

q: How does the book describe fiat money?
a: Fiat means let it be done on faith—value while everyone agrees. Crises flicker that faith and drain savings. Loans create new money; interest isn't fully created, so more is always owed than made. Not guilt: what we made together, we can unmake.

q: What is the musical chairs metaphor?
a: Debt-money like musical chairs: principal without interest printed—one chair too few—so someone loses home or livelihood. Walk out; build a room with a chair for everyone. Metaphor for money—not claiming Qortal is party entertainment.

Won when the last person neither must nor wants to sell minted QORT—QORT priceless as time. Everyone wins together. Checkmate for money-only systems; doorway to #QQQ. Metaphorical victory, not a console ending.

Stay synchronized; mint time; help loved ones; teach them. Spend #QQQ freely. Aim for the day no one needs to sell QORT. All for one, one for all. Game means shared voluntary practice—not a commercial video title.
No. Not one. Think metaphysics nonsense and still mint, hold keys, use an unswitchable internet. Philosophy is why he does it—not a toll. Skeptics wanting honest private life are equally welcome.

When I AM looks from every face, forgiveness is quiet recognition there was never truly someone else to blame. Prefer looking: who reads these words now? Forgive yourself first. In crisis, reach trusted people or local support—companion, not replacement for care.

Grief is not a mistake—love with nowhere to land; take all the time needed. Critique marketplace of grief, not seekers. Hold something beside grief: death as out-breath for life. Crisis or suicidal? Human support or emergency services—not a crisis line here.

q: Meaning of life in the book?
a: Meaning is made in what we do, not found. Whether you think you can or can't, you are right. Mistakes teach. New Earth: be happy now; leave the world lovelier. If unbearable, talk to someone you trust; you are not alone.

Treat neighbour as yourself—literally. Divine name: I AM—bare awareness never absent, looking from every face. Cruelty stops making sense; compassion remains. Prefer not believing—look. Invitation, not dogma.

Support a local farmer; plant a garden; keep animals if you can; revive markets; offer QORT sometimes; share qortal.dev or the book. Fake it until you make it—sharing never fake. Garden, neighbor, node, kindness.

In everyday philosophy, love is sustained care that seeks another’s good — not only feeling, but attention, honesty, and responsibility over time. Romance is one form; friendship, family, and chosen community are others. Healthy love respects boundaries and agency; control dressed as passion is not love. On Qortal themes, love shows up as contribution and stewardship rather than possession.
